item.title: Spain: General strike over housing costs before national election
item.description: Millions of Spanish workers shut down businesses and public transportation in a protest on Wednesday over housing costs that the government hopes to leverage before a national election later this month. The walkout — under the slogan “Salaries. Housing. Prices.” — was the first general strike in Spain in 14 years.

item.title: Exclusive: EU's Kallas says US 'can't negotiate on our behalf' on lifting Russia sanctions
item.description: In an exclusive interview with FRANCE 24, the EU's top diplomat Kaja Kallas discusses the war in Ukraine, the situation in the Middle East and a possible change in US President Donald Trump's foreign policy following the US midterm elections. The former Estonian prime minister, who is now the European Union's High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, also reaffirms the EU's position as a major player on the global geopolitical stage.

item.title: Charlotte Gainsbourg brings pioneering French lawyer Gisèle Halimi to the screen
item.description: New French film "Women on trial" revisits the landmark case in 1972 that paved the way for abortion legislation in France. Critic Manon Kerjean tells us why performances from Charlotte Gainsbourg and Cécile de France carry this powerful courtroom drama and how its directors recreated the tension of a high-profile social and legal battle.

item.title: Behind Georges Larnicol's creative spin on Breton specialty kouign-amann
item.description: From a traditional Breton specialty to an imaginative, bite-sized creation, in Entre Nous we explore how French pastry chef Georges Larnicol has reinvented the famous kouign-amann while preserving its Breton identity. He tells us what makes the pastry so special and why it is much loved around the world.

item.title: UNICEF head Catherine Russell: 'We're all committed to the importance of children'
item.description: More than 50 countries, 20 non-governmental and philanthropic organisations and a series of multinational companies are pledging this week to put children's rights at the heart of their policies and actions. A pact is being agreed upon at the Paris Peace Forum, where the rights of children are taking centre stage.
